newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon holds runoffs for second house of parliament.
newsitem.headline: Gabon holds runoffs for second house of parliament.

text.p: Gabon's municipal and regional councillors voted on Sunday in runoffs for the 91-seat senate, a new second house of parliament designed to promote a balance of power in the Central African nation, officials said.
President Omar Bongo's Democratic Party held 43 seats after a January 26 first round of voting, its allies seven, the opposition Woodcutters Rally 12 and other opposition parties six.

The polls are part of constitutional and electoral reforms launched after the oil-producing nation's political rivals struck a 1994 deal in Paris to defuse bloody political unrest following Bongo's disputed 1993 election.
Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of founding head of state, Leon Mba. He bowed to pressure for democratic reform in 1990.

Under the constitution, amended and approved by referendum in 1995, the national assembly and senate vote on all new laws. A joint commission will try to resolve any differences. In the event of deadlock, the national assembly takes precedence.
Bongo's supporters won 100 of the national assembly's 120 seats in December elections. The opposition fared better in October municipal polls, particularly in the capital.
